steps: Hearth & ember protection
Non-combustible masonry hearth 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the opening. Ember protection over combustible floor: 16" (USA) / 18" (Canada) from the glass, 8" each side.

The fireplace's non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the existing fireplace opening.

Combustible flooring in front needs ember protection: USA 16" to the firing side (from the glass) and 8" to each side of the door opening; Canada 18" and 8" to each side of the unit (p. 17).

The minimum fireplace opening is shown as a dimensioned drawing (Figure 11) on this page.
Clearances to combustibles
From the side of the door: 13" to an adjacent sidewall, 9-1/2" to side facing (max 3-1/2" deep). From the top: 13" to mantel facing and to a mantel max 12" deep.
Prepare the fireplace & chimney

Masonry wood-burning fireplace only, chimney 15' minimum from the hearth. Sweep, inspect and repair first; lock the damper open or remove it; fasten the metal tag to the back wall if the fireplace was modified.

• Masonry fireplace built to N.F.P.A. 211 or local codes; installation to CAN/CSA-B365. Not in a factory-built fireplace, and never a makeshift or temporary installation.
  • Have the chimney swept and inspected; check for creosote, obstructions, cracks or loose mortar, and complete repairs before installing.
  • Lock the damper open or remove it. Don't remove bricks or mortar, except masonry or steel (including the damper plate) from the smoke shelf and damper frame if needed for a liner, without weakening the structure or reducing protection for combustibles.
  • Fasten the supplied metal tag to the back wall if the fireplace was modified.
  • Don't connect to a flue serving another appliance. Mobile homes: not in a sleeping room.
  • The insert is heavy: install with two people, with cardboard or a heavy blanket on the hearth.
Feed the liner
Measure from the top of the chimney flue to the hearth floor, allowing for flashing and rain cap. Feed the stainless liner down through the damper area and fit a stove-to-liner adapter.

Full liner (required in Canada): measure from the top of the existing chimney flue to the floor of the hearth, leaving extra liner for flashing and rain cap. Feed the stainless steel liner from the top of the chimney, through the damper area and into the fireplace cavity, and attach a stove-to-liner adapter per the liner manufacturer's instructions.

Direct flue connection (USA only, p. 21): measure from the top of the first chimney flue liner tile to the top of the insert, allowing extra to insert into the tile. Feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile, fit the adapter, and seal where the liner passes through the chimney throat. A clean-out door may be required by local codes.
Attach the flue collar
The 6" I.D. collar is packed in the stove. Fix it to the liner adapter with three stainless screws, caulk the connections with high temp stove cement, and check that its gasket is in good shape.
Set & level the insert
Push the insert into the fireplace and level it with the front or rear adjustment legs (nuts in the bottom sides, front and rear).

Leveling legs (bolts) are supplied to level or steady the insert on an uneven hearth. If the fireplace is lower than the hearth, prop the unit up, thread the bolts into the inserts under the sides toward the rear, and set them to the depth of the drop (p. 17). Push the insert into position and adjust the bolts to level it.

For outside combustion air, don't cover the air inlet opening (p. 22).
Pull down & secure the collar

Remove the baffle and the flue gas agitator, reach through the flue opening and pull the collar down with the tool provided until its bolts pass through the mounting slots. Fit clamps and nuts, center, tighten.

1. Remove the baffle (p. 13): slide the ceramic board forward, remove the retaining pin at the back, lift the baffle off the supply tube, then move it aside and tilt it down and out.
  2. Remove the pre-installed flue gas agitator, which has to come out to install the flue collar (p. 15): lift it, pull it toward the front, and lower it out of the front mounting slots in the flame shield.
  3. Reach through the flue opening and pull the flue collar down with the tool provided until the bolts pass through the mounting slots. Install the clamps and nuts, center the collar on the opening and tighten the nuts.
  4. Refit the agitator and baffle in reverse order. The side blankets must be tight against the side rails and the ceramic board tight against the baffle.
Don't operate with the agitator, baffle assembly, tubes or insulation removed.
Flash & cap the chimney
Measure, trim and shape the chimney top flashing with a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side, seat it firmly against the flue tile, then attach the rain cap (storm collar optional).
Combustion air & power

Room air is drawn in through the bottom of the unit. For outside air, replace the ash clean-out cover with a rodent screen and seal the surround to the fireplace face. Grounded three-prong outlet; cord away from the unit.

Consult local building codes on combustion air.

  • Room air: the unit draws combustion air in through its bottom.
  • Outside air: remove the cover from the ash clean-out in the existing fireplace and put a rodent screen in its place. Don't cover the air inlet opening, then seal the surround to the fireplace face and anywhere else air may enter, so combustion air is drawn from outside into the intake on the bottom of the appliance.

Power: properly grounded outlet for a three-pronged plug; don't cut or remove the grounding prong; don't route the cord under the unit or against hot or sharp surfaces (p. 23). When refitting the blower assembly, route the power supply and thermocouple wires behind the tab on the casing bottom and up above the intake & control assembly without pinching them (p. 24).
Assemble & fit the surround
Bolt the top and sides together face down, fit the brow, slide the surround over the unit and ash shelf onto the side brackets, and push the insert back until the surround meets the fireplace face.

1. Lay the top and sides face down on a flat, non-marring surface and fasten them with the 1/4" x 1/2" bolts and nuts provided.
  2. Stand it upright and check the front face is flat and even at the joints and sides.
  3. Secure the brow to the underside of the surround top with the four 1/4"-20 X 1/2" hex screws and nuts; keep it straight and even with the top.
  4. Slide the surround over the unit and ash shelf, engaging the tabs on its inside back into the slots in the surround brackets on the sides of the firebox.
  5. Push the entire appliance back until the surround is in contact with the fireplace face.

Optional battery backup (pp. 25-26): separate the barrel jack extension wire, load the batteries, place the box on the outside edge of the surround with the wires facing down, and plug its barrel jack into the side of the blower assembly.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Never use chemicals or any other volatile liquid to start a fire. Build the fire directly on the firebricks, with no grate or andirons.

  1. Slide the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre and crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it. Add a few pieces of large kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame. Never leave the insert unattended with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small pieces of wood and close the door.
  5. Begin normal operation once there is a good bed of coals and the wood has charred.
Your first 2-3 fires bake the paint on. Ventilate the room well and open all windows and doors, since the smoke and fumes can bother some people. Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sits beneath the ash lip, the shelf at the front of the insert. Facing the insert, it runs from Low on the right to High on the left. The middle can be considered Medium, and any position in between gives a different burn rate and heat output.

High (all the way left)Lighting, and charring fresh wood after you reload
Low (pushed to the far right)Overnight or extended burns

For a clean fire with little smoke, add small loads (two or three logs at a time, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load) and leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading. After 30 minutes or so you can turn it down a lot.

Don't over-fire. Don't run on High for long periods. A glowing red top or vent pipe means the insert is over-firing. That can permanently damage the insert and chimney and may void the warranty.

The minimum low burn rate is set at the factory and must not be changed. Wood type, outside temperature, chimney size and weather all change the right setting, so expect some practice.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
Reloading

  1. Slide the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff out into the room.
  3. Load wood parallel to the front, placed so air can flow between the logs. Don't load it so high that opening the door would be hazardous.
  4. Burn on High for about 10 - 15 minutes or until the wood is fully charred, then set the air where you want it.

Overnight

Unsplit logs work best. Char the wood completely on High, then slowly turn the air control to Low. Don't try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting from hot coals

  1. Open the door and rake the hot embers toward the front. Add a couple of dry, split logs on top and close the door.
  2. Set the air to High. The logs should begin burning within a few minutes.
  3. Once the wood has charred, reset the air control.

Fire won't last the night? Set the air lower, use more wood (unsplit is best), and have the door gasket checked.

wood.title: Choosing your wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood generally gives higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwood or green wood. Season it for six months or more and store it under cover, away from open flame or heat sources.

Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good, large bed of coals:

  • Dry: burning on more than one side within one minute.
  • Damp: turns black and lights within three minutes.
  • Soaked: sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Salt water wood, wet or green wood, unseasoned wood, treated wood, garbage, coal or charcoal, cardboard or other paper products, plywood, particleboard, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, construction or demolition debris, manure or animal remains, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners, asphalt products, solvents, or anything containing plastic, rubber (including tires) or asbestos. Burning these may release toxic fumes, or make the insert ineffective and cause smoke. Salt water wood and garbage contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

Note: p. 6 lists wet or green wood and unseasoned wood among the things not to burn. p. 8 says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and not to attempt to burn overnight using green or wet wood.
Note: the manual gives the maximum log length as 17 inches on p. 3 and up to 18" on p. 7. The ideal length is 16 inches.

glass.title: Glass & door care
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the insert is cold, with fireplace glass cleaner. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape with anything that could scratch it.

What the deposit tells you

  • Light brown and dusty, wipes off easily: good combustion and dry wood, so the pipes and chimney are likely fairly clean.
  • Black and greasy, hard to remove: wet or green wood and too slow a burn. It is building up at least as fast in the chimney.

Glass that keeps getting dirty usually means wet wood, turning the air down before there is a good bed of coals and charred wood, low draft, or a leaking door gasket.

Door care

  • Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass.
  • Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the insert. Use only ceramic glass from your dealer.
  • Clean the plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.
  • Check the door gasket weekly for sagging, placement and damage. Your dealer has the replacement kit (part 80000670).

ash.title: Removing the ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the insert is cold.

  • When ashes are 3" to 4" deep in the firebox, let the fire burn down and cool, then remove the excess.
  • Leave about 1" of ash on the firebox bottom. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Keep the front of the firebox, where the boost combustion air comes in, clear of heavy ash so it doesn't block the airflow.

Disposing of ashes

Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn. If you will bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all cinders have thoroughly cooled. Don't put other waste in that container.

blower.title: The blower & power outages
blower.html:
The insert has a variable-speed blower that circulates warm air. It has a rocker switch and a fan speed control.

Rocker OFF: automaticTurns on once the insert reaches operating temperature, and off after the fire is out and it has cooled
Rocker ON: manualBypasses the temperature switch so you have full control

In either mode, set the fan speed control where you like. With the air control on Low (pushed to the far right), run the blower on Low. With the air control anywhere above Low, use any speed you want.

Power outages

Without power, the insert still runs within safe and certified limits on its manual air control. An optional battery backup (part 11490005) keeps it fully functional during an outage.

Keep it clean

Vacuum the blower's grill openings at least every six months to clear dust and pet hair. Disconnect power before servicing.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar and vapours that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If creosote ignites, it burns extremely hot: that's a chimney fire.

Keep it clean

  • Inspect the chimney and connector at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it is 3 mm or more.
  • Check daily until you learn how often you need to clean. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Burn dry wood, and don't turn the air down too soon after loading.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Get everyone ready to evacuate, with a meeting place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the insert.
  3. Call the fire department, and have a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Before your next fire, the chimney must be cleaned and checked for stress and cracks. Also check combustibles around the chimney and the roof.
Before the chimney is swept, the flue thermocouple (a sensor whose tip sits in the flue opening) must be pulled out using its guide behind the surround, then pushed back in afterwards.

safety.title: Safety around the insert
safety.html:
• The insert is hot while it runs, especially the glass and outer surfaces. Keep children, clothing and furniture away, and never let children touch the glass.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning, and open it only to add wood. The insert isn't designed for open-door burning.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep them well away.
  • Burn only wood. Charcoal and other fuels can produce large amounts of carbon monoxide.
  • Don't store wood or other combustibles within the installation clearances or the space you need for loading.
  • Don't alter the air control assembly. Tampering voids the warranty and could be very hazardous.
Pacific Energy strongly recommends smoke and carbon monoxide detectors in the area where the insert is installed. Make sure everyone in your home knows how to run it safely and what to do in a chimney fire.
Watch the draft. Draft is the force that moves air from the insert up the chimney. An uncontrollable burn, or a stove part or chimney glowing red, means too much draft. Smoke leaking into the room through the joints means too little.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's Limited Lifetime warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 Year Comprehensive, parts and laborAny defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage
  • Firebox rails and heat shields (not in the lifetime warranty)
  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets
  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification

Early wear points to improper use, such as excessive draft, heating too large an area, or fuel with high sodium content, plastics or chemicals, and may void the warranty.

Making a claim

Contact your dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. You can register the insert at pacificenergy.net/register; the serial number is on the certification label or the manual cover.

specOutput.title: Emissions, efficiency & output
specOutput.html:
EPA certified emissions1.6 grams per hour
LHV tested efficiency82%
HHV tested efficiency75%
EPA BTU output13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr
Maker's website: Heat Output (Cord Wood) 56,000 BTU.
CO emissions1.4 grams per minute

Meets the 2020 EPA crib wood particulate emission standards (test Method 28R). Efficiencies are weighted averages per CSA B415; the BTU range comes from the low and high EPA tests using Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. The rating statement on the same page rounds it to 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr.

The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered.

specFuel.title: Wood length & fuel
specFuel.html:
Maximum wood length (p. 3)17 inches
Ideal wood length16 inches
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Note: the manual gives the maximum wood length as 17 inches in the efficiency table on p. 3 and up to 18" (457mm) in Normal Operation on p. 7.
Maker's website: Log Size (max) 17".

Cordwood only. Load parallel to the stove front with space for air between logs; burn directly on the firebricks with no grate or andirons.

specFlue.title: Flue, liner & chimney
specFlue.html:
Flue collar6" I.D., removable (packed in the stove)
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)
Recommended flue draft.06" - .09" w.c. when hot, on high
  • Canada: full flue liner required, continuous from the flue collar to the top of the chimney, meeting class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640.
  • USA: flue liner conforming to UL-1777, or a direct flue connection assembly. Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner for correct draft and to prevent difficult start-ups and smoking out the door.
  • Direct flue connection (USA only): liner runs into the first chimney flue tile; a seal must be provided in the chimney throat, and local codes may require a clean-out door.

Lock the existing damper open or remove it. Don't connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.

specHearth.title: Hearth & ember protection
specHearth.html:
Hearth (p. 16): the fireplace's non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the existing fireplace opening. The rating label adds: install only on a non-combustible hearth under the unit, extending 16 in (406 mm) in front of the fireplace opening face.

Ember protection: combustible flooring in front of the insert must be protected by non-combustible material extending:

USA16" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the door opening
Canada18" (457 mm) to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the unit

Codes: CAN/CSA-B365 in Canada, N.F.P.A. 211 in the USA. The minimum fireplace opening is shown only as a dimensioned drawing (Figure 11, p. 16), and the ember-protection layout as Figure 12 on this page.

Figure 12 (p. 17) labels the Canadian 18" as 406mm; the rating label (p. 3) gives 457 MM / 18 IN for Canadian ember protection.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Rating label (p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP
Installation (p. 19)120V, 60 Hz, 2.2 A
Blowers (p. 23)120V, 60 Hz, 1A
Note: the rating label (p. 3) gives the electrical rating as 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP; p. 19 says the unit must be plugged into a standard wall outlet for 120V, 60 Hz, 2.2 A; and the Blowers section (p. 23) gives an electrical rating of 120V, 60 Hz, 1A.

Use a properly grounded outlet that accepts a three-pronged plug; don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Route the cord away from the unit, never under it, and clear of hot or sharp surfaces. Wire to local codes, or CSA C22.2 (Canada) / ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA). Disconnect power before servicing.

Power failure: the insert still operates within safe and certified limits on the manual air control. The optional battery backup (11490005) keeps it fully functional.

specSurround.title: Surround dimensions
specSurround.html:
Regular surround (11250047)A 37" / 965mm · B 28" / 710mm
Oversized surround (11250048)A 42" / 1070mm · B 30" / 760mm

A and B are lettered dimensions on the drawing (Figure 7) on this page. The insert's own dimensions are given only on that drawing; the text confirms a 6" I.D. removable flue collar.

The surround is pushed back against the fireplace face; for outside combustion air, seal it to the face (p. 22).

specParts.html:

The baffle removal steps (p. 13) print the gasket between baffle and supply tube as prt#80000365; the parts list (p. 31) has no 80000365 and lists Gasket, 2" Baffle Tube, 10 pack as 80000356.

Maintenance checks (p. 12)

  • Weekly: firebrick for cracking; door gasket for sagging, placement, damage.
  • Monthly: brick rail tabs and rails, air riser tube, back of the airwash chamber, baffle locking pin, baffle tubes, boost tube cover.
  • At chimney cleaning: top baffle board / blanket, baffle, top heat shield and bolts, baffle gasket, brick rails, manifold. Pull the flue thermocouple out with its guide first and push it back after (pp. 8-9).
  • Blower: vacuum the grill openings at least every six months.

Baffle warping up to 1/4" is normal; replace if greater, cracked or broken. Use only manufacturer-supplied materials. Firebrick sizes and layout: pp. 28-30.

Shown only as drawings and not transcribed: insert dimensions (Figure 7, p. 14; text states only the 6" I.D. removable flue collar), minimum fireplace opening (Figure 11, p. 16), clearance drawing incl. an unexplained 34 3/8" / 840mm value (Figure 13, p. 18), ember-protection drawing values CAN 20 5/8" / 610mm and USA 18 5/8" (Figure 12, p. 17), firebrick layout and brick counts (Figure 23, p. 28), wiring diagram (Figure 16, p. 23) and parts diagram (p. 32). Surround A/B values come from the text table on p. 14; what A and B measure is shown only in Figure 7. The manual gives no firebox volume, weight, heating area, burn time, cordwood maximum BTU, blower cfm, viewing area or catalytic/non-catalytic statement, so catalog fields firebox_cu_ft, heating_area_sqft_max, burn_time_hr_max, btu_output_cordwood_max, glass_area_sq_in/view_area, combustion_type and the cfm/ACMS feature claims could not be checked. Catalog log_length_max_in matches p. 3 but p. 7 differs (see conflicts and catalog_mismatches). The parts list and wiring show a control board and flue/firebox thermocouples, but the manual does not describe any automatic combustion control, so the guide doesn't. Battery type for the optional battery box is not stated. The rating statement (p. 3) gives 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr vs 13,494 to 23,186 in the table: treated as rounding, both shown. Minor: p. 2 text and the label footer say VISTA INSERT LE; p. 16 cites Figure 73 and p. 18 cites Figure 12 for drawings that are Figures 11 and 13; the parts list skips item 6 and the diagram shows an item 42 that is not listed; blower cleaning is described as the back and bottom grill openings (p. 12) and the front grill (p. 23). The warranty labels the limited lifetime coverage (10 years); reproduced as printed. Pages 34-35 are blank. Label is bilingual; English text used, no French-only content. Oct 12: the website's Heat Output (Cord Wood) and Log Size (max) are shown as Maker's website notes (specOutput, specFuel). website.json prints no output range, so the catalog's btu_output_min/max figures are not quoted in the guide.
